#54538 22 2005-03-17T17:55:51Z nevermore
You mean right here?:

Curve kick:
Similar to the corner kick. You run up to an 8 curve, or one that bulges at you. Just like in the corner kick, jump so that you nick the edge of the curve. Right as you touch, jump again and hold it. This isn't as effective as the corner kick, but still makes you fly.

Bounceblock:
You need to at least somewhat understand how bounceblocks work before you attempt this.
Jump onto a bounceblock and let it go pretty low. It goes lower if you move to the side when you land on it, so if you can, alternate pushing the left and right keys rapidly. If you can't manage that, just try to stay on the block while slightly moving. After the bounceblock reaches its lowest point and starts to come up, press jump twice quickly, but not too fast.

Oneway wall jump: (I only am gonna do this, because the others really aren't used in the highscores)
This one is pretty easy. If you are on a wall that has a oneway facing down towards you, walljump up the wall. Try to time your jumps so that your last one gets you right under the oneway. If you manage to pull it off right, when you jump again, you should go through the oneway. It all depends on how close you are to the oneway.

I was playing Tenacious, and I decided I really like it. The beginning is the hardest part, which is always a good thing. There's a tougher all gold challenge, which is a definite plus. It's very hard, but also quite original, which is quite good. Finally, you went out on a limb. You made a decision to make it really hard, and people might or might not have liked it at all.
So that's my two pennies.

Daddaluma, I just posted two demos, and I found the technique. It's all in where and how you land. You can't land on the hole. Land on the slope and hold right. You should stay one it for a second, then sort of skip off. You've got to time it so that when you skip off you land in the opening. That momentum is what pushes you halfway through. Once your almost there, sometimes it just shoots you out on the other side, but sometimes you have to do some work. Halfway through hold left, so that you go against the tile. It should work after practice.
Of course, the buttons are switched at the second *tight* squeeze.

Yeah, I think it has something to do with the same effect that makes you go through a locked door if there's a jump pad below. If there were an extra frame it wouldn't let the rocket go through you, but because you just jumped to the other side of the rocket, it doesn't affect you.

Think. If a rocket shoots at you and you hit a teleporter that shoots you across where the rocket is, the rocket won't hit you. That's because the computer onlyrecognizes the frames that are there. Does that make sense?

Recently I found something that was even stranger. If you are wallsliding, a rocket can fit between you and the wall, and actually thread right between you! I had a hold left DDA that illustrated this, but it's gone with the rest of my computer.

I have a little challenge for you, but I don't want to create a new thread. My little brother and I made it, and I can assure you every goal is possible.
The aim:
1. Get all of the lasers to be firing at one time
2. Complete the level
3. Complete it in under 600 frames
4. Get a little amount of gold.

You start with 100 points, and you get 3 points off for each piece of gold you pick up. If you get all of the lasers firing, you get 10 points. If you complete the level, you get 10 points. If you complete it in under 600 frames, you get 25 points.
So go!

We do have this Maths Challenge thing. The prize for doing well in one round is that you get to do another one.

They were less straight maths questions, and more puzzles that you needed maths skills to solve. Things like:

If you start with this string:

"MI"

And you have these rules:

You can add "U" to any string that ends in "I"
You can change "Mx" to "Mxx" (you can double anything that comes after M)
You can change "III" to "U"
You can change "UU" to nothing.

Prove whether you can or cannot produce the string "MU"

Or something like that, anyway. As I remember, they were fairly open ended questions like that. Proving things about prime numbers, that kinda stuff. Not done one for years though, too much bother.

MIIU

MIIII
MIU
MIIUU
ARGH! It's not possible!

MI

#59814 208 2005-04-12T23:16:34Z nevermore
Map: Framework
Author: tktktk

First of all, I would just like to say that I had more fun playing this map than I have with almost any other map. That said, I have to adress the theme. Now, metanet maps usually have a nice flow, without only one obvious route. Definitely present in this map. They also have tileset themes/patterns a lot of the time, which you also included (framework). I actually enjoyed the length of this, and the placement of the gold was very well thought out. The drone paths were also very metanet-y. My problem was the lack of simplicity. Many metanet maps are long, but this was a bit more complex than most of them. But this was just a minor problem.
Score: 47/50

Map: N Your Eyes
Author: Kablizzy

Another really nice map. I loved the simplicity of this map, and yet how it was still interesting. It's somewhat easy, like a metanet map, and the tiles are wonderfully done. The level has a nice flow, although it could have been improved in the middle section. The drones were used very well, and the thwumps were a very interesting addition. I loved playing this map, but once again the flow might need some work. Overall, this is a really fun map that for the most part looks and plays like a metanet map.
Score: 44/50

Map: Amun's Revenge
Author: Kablizzy

I had a lot of fun playing this map, and a lot of it was absolutely stellar. I thought some things were really done with metanet in mind, specifically the floor guards, the mine fields, and the arena. I had a couple of problems with this, though. First of all, this map didn't look quite as good as it played out. Of course, aesthetics aren't everything, but they have an effect on the way a level feels, and the factor of if this would fit into the real game. I also had a bit of a problem with the gold placement. Parts just felt very awkward, and the style of placement was somewhat inconsistent. Also, one of those switches seems to be useless (the one at the bottom left). This is still a very fun level, with some kinks to work out.
Score: 40/50

I'm going to submit these scores now. I don't want to submit them all at once, because I'm worried that my computer might crash. More coming tonight.

#59837 210 2005-04-13T02:09:53Z nevermore
Map: Simplistic Confusion
Author: Makron

First of all, congratulations on getting this into N v1.4. So, now for the judging. This map was really fun, and I liked how it was quite easy. I can tell you tried to work in some metanet techniques, while giving it your own flair, for lack of a better word. A few words on the tileset: It looks pretty cool, but not at all like a metanet level. Lucky for you, the tileset really worked, and was a major part of the gameplay. I feel you might have strayed from the theme a bit, because you wanted to create an original, fun level, and that you succeeded in. Overall this is quite a fun map that has a metanet flow, but not a metanet feel.

Score: 37/50


Map: Sudden Diversion
Author: Makron

Another easy, fun level by you. This one shows your style too, but I feel like you may have strayed from the original theme too much here. Metanet maps are more about (with some exceptions, of course) their simplicity, and the many different possible routes. This one is quite simple, which I appreciate, but cavern levels usually don't have many possibilities. I could tell, while I played it, that you intended for a certain route to be taken. Also, caverns usually aren't in the real game. This is still quite a fun level, but maybe not right for this competition.

Score: 36/50[/color]

Map: Shelter
Author: stepself

I liked playtesting this map, and the tileset's really interesting. Your use of the chaingun drone and the rocket launchers were very metanetish, but the mines could have used some work. Some of the pieces of gold were a bit unacessable (sp?), and I'm sort of "iffy" about the one way. Overall, it's quite an entertaining level, with some tweaks needed.

Score: 42/50


Map: Adding
Author: holy_trinity/Igi/And

This was another fun map, however the tileset seemed a bit lacking of a pattern. You seemed to master the use of certain enemies, but the pluses are sort of binding and a bit too claustrophobic. Also, it seemed a bit repetitive in a sense. I found I was using the same techniques again and again. All in all, this level has a really nice feel, but some work could be done on the tileset and gameplay.

Score: 36/50


Map: Pleh
Author: Echarin

I didn't expect this map to have a metanet flair, however, you proved me wrong. Granted, it is lacking some sort of pattern, unlike most levels in the real game, but it flows pretty much perfectly as a metanet level. Now, I did have a few problems. The left side felt a bit off... I'm not sure what, just something felt wrong. Also, the rocket placement could have been a bit more exact and considerate for the player. To sum it up, this level has an accurate representation of a metanet flow, but unfortunately some parts felt rushed.

Score: 43/50


Map: Fluidity
Author: Lancer0

This one convinced me. As soon as I saw it, I understood what you were going for. This is a tremendous representation of metanet levels. Simple levels with side gold challenges. There are many levels like this in early episodes, and I wouldn't mind if this were traded for one of those. I really feel like this tackled the spirit of this competition, and you added your own little touch.

Score: 48/50

Map: Pulvonary
Author: stepself

Alright, off the bat this really looks like a metanet level. It looks very similar to an already existing level, which may or may not have been by accident.
Now, I really like how it looks. Aesthetically, the gold gives it a nice touch, and it's a very interesting tileset. The flow is nice, but sometimes the thwump gets in the way. When it works, it really works, but sometimes I either go too fast, and the thwump doesn't come back up the second time, or I go to slowly, and the thwump goes too fast. Also, I'm not quite sure about the bounceblock/mine combination at the bottom. It's tough to deal with.
Overall, the enemies here all work very well, however the thwump isn't always reliable.

Score: 38/50


Map: Math
Author: holy_trinity/And/Igi

I don't really like the tileset. It just doesn't seem metanetty. Sure, it has a theme, but it's not as concentrated on the gameplay as most metanet levels are. I like the placement of the drones, and not once did I feel frustrated when I died to one of them. The rockets were pretty annoying, though. A lot of the time I felt that there was no way to avoid death, which I usually don't feel in the real game.Gold placement was fine, but a bit linear, and the level had a surprisingly nice feel. It's a pretty nice level, but somewhat sloppy and not quite metanety.

Score: 30/50


Map: Up, up, and... run away!
Author: Brickman

I've got to give you props on the tileset. I just feel the metanet vibe. The turrets were nice, and kept me moving more than I'd expect, just like many metanet levels. The area with the rocket was a bit confusing... I originally thought you were supposed to jump through the small gap. The middle section was also quite confusing. I kept going up the wrong side, realizing, and having to go back and try again. The part with the floorgaurds was actually quite interesting, especially the top guard, but I just couldn't see it in a metanet level. It's pretty much a good level, with some issues with clarity.

Score: 35/50

#62241 223 2005-04-26T23:06:41Z nevermore
*whines*
Maniac, please get us the list.

Map: Defenscerrator
Author: Eli

Ok, you start off the level safe. That is almost always a good thing. Then come the problems. Slopes generally aren't used that way in metanet levels. I can say there really aren't many slope jumping maps that aren't user made in the game. Also, the tileset seems very awkward. The [e] tiles mixed with the slopes. It all just seems very hectic.
The switches are hard to get, because it's hard to get into each compartment. Then you completely change the flow of the level into a bounceblock jumping level. The laser seems somewhat randomly placed, and is quite aggravating.
I'm not sure why those oneways were placed. They don't seem to add to the level at all.
Also, the gold is waaay out of your way, which is a problem. Usually metanet levels give you the opportunity to get the gold, with some difficulty. Getting the gold in this level is mostly just a distraction, and creates a whole new level.
So, overall it's quite a messy map which ranges from being easy to very hard.

Score: 26/50


Map: Alternate
Author: Kablizzy

The tileset is nice, but the middle seems quite off. Something about the center glob just seems... misfitting. While playing this level, not once did I feel frustrated, which is also nice. Instead of really making us work, you gave the flow right to us. The drones were distracting, and when the posed a threat it usually ended in waiting around for a long time. This usually isn't done in metanet levels. I like the turrets, they add to the level, but the gold placement irks me a bit. Especially in the middle left and right. All gold probably isn't happening -- at least if someone tried to get all gold they'd lose time rather than gaining it. The thwump at the beginning and the mines on the cieling didn't really serve a purpose, but that's pretty minor.
Overall, I enjoyed the simplicity of this level, even though it had a few problems.

Score: 38/50


Map: Coulomb
Author: newt

Patterny tilesets are good. The tileset is cool, interesting design. Going up the left side is pretty easy, I got that my first try. I could definitely see something like that in the real game. The right side is a different story. Slope jumping isn't very metanetty, especially when if you miss, you have to climb back up again. Also, the drones really annoyed me. I would open up a chamber to get at a switch, and a drone would enter just before I got there, making me wait. The trapdoors seemed a bit unnecessary, especially the second. After getting the second one, I never even went back to the right side. The gold placement looked nice, but on the left it seemed unrealistic to acquire - once again, someone might lose time rather than gaining it.
Overall, it's a nice looking level with some kinks to iron out.

Score: 35/50


Map: Chambers Net(net)ine
Author: Eli

Let us start with the small things. Aesthetics. It looks very nice, aside from a couple of pieces of gold embedded in the walls. One complaint - usually metanet fills up their tiles, but there are definite exceptions (8-0 comes to mind). Also, I try to stick with this with all of my maps - more than one door next to each other doesn't look nice, and is rarely (possibly never) done in metanet maps. I really like how you can use the curves to your advantage, and avoiding the rockets is a blast. However, some of the locked doors were very unnecessary, and I feel this level might have used some more playtesting.
Overall it's really quite fun, with some metanet problems.

Score: 38/50

Whew. Gotta go study for a history test.

I've been wanting to show you guys a piece of my writing for a little while now, but I haven't really had anything that really showed my writing style, because of my stolen computer. So in English class recently we were supposed to write a piece that focused on one moment spanning from 3-5 minutes. This is my outcome. It's somewhat morbid, but bear with it.

Quote: Moment Piece
I looked behind me for a mement, only to see the two snarling figures hot on my trail. All I could make out was their metallic-blue eyes peering through the bare, snow-dusted trees. How strange that those two things so evil could come from such beauty as the forest. The contrast was intriguing, and I almost stopped running just to stare. The two beasts gained on me, and the beads of eyes started to become much, much bigger. I could now make out their figures and knew they weren't ugly at all. In fact, they were devilishly beautiful.
They were two hybrid creatures, a mixture of what seemed to be a wolf and a stag. Their bodies were furry and slender, and they were quite agile; they were perfectly shaped and trained machines to attack. Their legs came out of their body very thick and wide, with obviously distinguished muscles, and were quite long, and as your eyes traveled to the foot, you would see the leg become thinner and thinner, finally expanding for the hoof. Their necks were very thick, a combination of the hair's fluffiness, and the very solid muscles to hold their long antlers up. As they ran, their fur was pushed back and rippled by the wind, creating an arrow-like effect. But the features that stood out the most were their eyes. They were as blue as the sky, and if you looked straight into them, you could feel them peering into your soul, evaluating and judging you, bit by bit. And they were vibrant.
As I ran, I started to tire out. I was barefoot and almost naked, and both the brambles and twigs on the ground and the cold wind cut into my skin and cause extreme pain. I leaned over and picked up some bark from the ground and attempted to cover myself. I shivered and breathed a white puff of breath. As it rose through the atmosphere it was like an angel ascending to heaven. Finally it expanded and dissappeared, and my visualization was lost. My hope was lost. I had no more strength, and couldn't go on. The beasts could do their worst on me, no matter the pain. I would leave this life of misery and grief, and face the unknown.
I looked at the ground rushing by me and tried to time my fall. I was already in so much pain, and I knew that if I didn't fall safely, I would probably die. I looked ahead of me, and saw a pile of snow near a tree. I didn't think; I didn't want to think. I closed my eyes and jumped.
I didn't even feel the impact. I just felt the cold snow rub against my open wounds. I didn't care. I would let them do their worst. I was limp, and could barely see anything but two blurry figures approaching rapidly, and I didn't care. I would let them do their worst. They slowed down, and cautiously padded up. They reeked of excrement. I didn't care. I would let them do their worst. They poked at me with their snots, and pawed at my arms with their hoods, making sure I wasn't a threat. I didn't care. Their hoofs were surprisingly warm and smooth; perfect blunt weapons. I would let them do their worst. They both looked me in the eye, and that was the last thing I saw. I didn't care. I would let them do their worst.
I was blind now - I had to rely only on my ears to know what they were doing to me, for now my body was entirely numb. My arms and legs were probably broken, or at least sprained. Something cool and wet brushed against my leg. One of the animals was licking my leg clean. The other was brushing the snow off me with his antlers. I felt relaxed; I felt ready. As one of them fitted its teeth around my legs, I smiled, and almost laughed. To die would really be a great adventure.
My right leg was gone. I couldn't feel it anymore, and certainly couldn't move it. It was the only part of my body that was in extreme pain. I felt the ground with my hands, brushing against one of the creatures' feet. I quickly pulled away, and kept feeling around. Right next to me was a tree stump, and I leaned my head back to rest on it. I wasn't in any pain anymore now - I could just feel the blood clinging to my skin. As my blind eyes faced the sky, I started to see something. I saw darkness. Utter and complete darkness. And as the two monsters ripped at my flesh, the darkness was ripped away by little spots of light, as if somebody was sticking twigs through a dark sheet of cloth one by one. Slowly, a little white spot appeared in the middle of my line of vision, and started to grow so subtly and slowly that it was unseeable.
The dot grew bigger and bigger, and became a star, then an eye, then the moon, and the sun. I could feel my body getting lighter. My torso had less and less to support. The little dot of light had become enormous, and was filling my whole view. My legs started to get warm, and the sensation traveled up my body until it reached my head. I felt quite comfortable. All of a sudden the nice warmth shot away and was soon replaced by a chilling trickle down my spin. I shuddered at the iciness, and started to quietly moan. It became louder, and was at a scream. I was screaming at the top of my lungs. I screamed for what seemed like hours, but was probably seconds. Finally, I lost energy amd collapsed. I stopped screaming. I stopped hurting. I stopped being cold. I stopped being. I stopped.
I wasn't alive when the beasts were done with me, but I could still hear them softly. They growled at each other and howled in unison as I drifted off to a better place.
Feel free to comment and make suggestions.

#64043 231 2005-05-07T02:31:21Z nevermore
Judging coming soon. I was going to judge this past week, but I had forgotten about the trip to DC.


And here it is.

Map: Around the World
Author: Heartview

I really couldn't see myself beating this. The difficulty wasn't the problem - it was just way too much back an forth. The drone rooms were interesting, but too cramped, and I had some minor problems with the tileset, especially near the beginning.

Score: 29/50


Map: No gold no Glamour
Author: Echarin

This wasn't stylized enough for my tastes and metanet norms. Also, it was a bit too complex. I didn't like the gold placement at the top very much. The rockets worked well, but seemed to get on my nerves after a little while. I would say replace the oneways in the pillar with normal tiles, if I were king of the world.

Score: 34/50


Map: Wrench
Author: maximo

Off the bat I found it very hard, but it does get easier once you get the hang of it. To be honest, it isn't very metanet at all - possibly the tileset, although that felt a bit off to me too. I might have liked this more if the first time around were removed - it might remove some of the stress. Also, it might have been nice to be able to get back up if you fell. It's a nice map, but maybe too representative of your style to represent metanet style.

Score: 32/50


Map: eighttriggers
Author: rrrobyp

It's very nice. Very, very nice. I really like how you made it feel like a metanet level without copying anything already existing. I think the tileset was somewhat bare, and could have used more of a fullness, and that laser didn't quite fit in there. I'm not sure what would have been better, but the laser just irked me.
The rockets are good, but the area around the rockets aren't as nice. The gold placement over there seems a bit off, and the bounceblocks trap me a lot. But overall it's very enjoyable, and fits the guidelines quite well.

Score: 41/50


Map: N Ultra 64
Author: Daddaluma

It doesn't look very nice, and the tileset alone would stick out like a sore thumb if placed in the real game. However, certain areas really did feel like metanet. I think that those trap doors didn't fit very well, but maybe if you replaced the trap door switch with something else... I liked getting it right under the guass. The gold is just bothersome, but I guess in moderation it's fine to pick up.

Score: 30/50

Done for now!
*jumps on hyper star and flies off into the distance*

In debug mode, in tile edit mode, all of the grid lines work - except for [L]. [L] only works if another gridline is activated. In other words, if you go into tile edit mode with no gridline, and you try to turn the [L] one on, it doesn't.

Not true. Look at the replay data. For it the syntax is :

oh i see. i thought you had to have it in your data to be able to watch the replay. but how would the replay system know what level you want to watch, if it doesn't have the level in its database?

Ok, here goes.
The demo data that the user levels mode gives you has the map data built into it. Soooo, if you take a demo from debug mode and want to watch it in user level mode, you can manually edit it to include the level data too. So when the game reads the demo, it also reads the level data. It loads the level based off of the demo, regardless of if you have it in your database or not. Understand?

#65808 55 2005-05-14T18:10:15Z nevermore
I just beat it again. Let's take this step by step.

1. Get through the first corridor. You shouldn't have too much trouble with this.
2. You are now near that downward facing thwump. Jump above it, so it goes down below you.
3. Drop down and land on the tiny ledge opposite that lone piece of gold.
4. Let the thwump come up towards you to get it out of the way.
5. Drop down and hit the slope that has a piece of gold on it on the left, slowing you down.
6. Hit the edge of the slope at the bottom right, so that you make the two bottom thwumps move.
7. Wait for the rightward facing thwump to come close.
8. Jump up and slide on the back, walljumping regularly to make sure that you don't slip off.
9. When you reach the wall, jump off and chill in the little nook under the wall of mines.
10. Once you're psyched, jump up so that you're resting on the tip of the corner next to the wall of mines.
11. Quickly jump off of that ledge to the one up and to your right. You can chillax there for a little while to get ready for what comes next.
12. Jump and hook around the ledge above you so that the leftward facing thwump triggers.
13. Stay on the [1] tile until the thwump passes you. Then jump up and wallslide on the back of it.
13a. Stay on the back of the thwump. This can get tricky because you can get caught on a corner. The trick is is to wall jump right before you get to the corner - especially the one with the door switch.
14. Jump off of the thwump as you pass the corner on the cieling. Land on the closest slope from you, but make sure you don't go too far.
15. Wait for the thwump to your right to pass you.
16. Drop down and land in the area right under where the thwump was. The thwump on the left will come towards you.
17. Stay in the little corner for about a second, and then jump out and land directly to your left onto the [1] slope. The thwump on the left should be very close to you.
18. Jump back up the hallway you came from, letting the thwump pass right under you.
19. Land back on the slope, and quickly get ready to jump again.
20. Jump, so that you wallslide on the thwump that just passed you. Stay on it.
21. Jump off as you near the wall. Take a deep breath and stay here until you're ready for the most intense part.
22. Jump up and land on the slope to the right and above your head. Not the one near the thwump, but the one under that area.
23. Jump again and land on the slope in the area right next to the mine. You don't have very much room here because of the mine, so I suggest you move quickly.
24. Jump up and land on the _second_ slope away from you. It's much easier to maneuver from there than the closest slope, even though it's a bit of a harder jump.
25. Jump back up as soon as you land. If you time it right, the thwump will pass under you. But STILL BE ALERT!
26. This is the tricky part. Use the slope on the ceiling and a slight tapping of the right key to land right where you need to. In the little space between the two clusters of mines. If you make this jump, let go of your keyboard. You don't know how many times I've spazzed here and messed up.
27. Once you're calm, jump to your right, arcing up and landing gracefully in the exit.
Congrats.

I realized your first point mid post, but decided not to delete it all.

This brings me to my story. Everyone, gather 'round.
I live in Hong Kong for seven years when my parents tell me we were moving. A few weeks later I started getting the worst stomach cramps ever. Purely psychological. They came on in spurts, and I missed a few weeks of school. I got sonograms - my innards were very, very active. We went to the doctor's countless amounts of times, and there were no results. So finally, three weeks before we leave, we decide to take a different approach and visit a Chinese doctor. Not a doctor that is Chinese, but a traditional Chinese doctor. We go, he feels my pulse and my heart beat, then writes up a prescription. He doesn't even touch my stomach.
He gives us an assortment of herbal ingredients and tells us to create a tea out of them twice a week. There were twigs, pieces of birds nest (no joke), etc. And the tea was absolutely horrid. Two weeks later it went away.

#67427 5 2005-05-17T21:37:35Z nevermore
Alright, I think it's actually much easier not to get the switches that open the doors above the exit. It reduces playing time. So, assuming you've seen the highscores, you know you have to quickly jump into the tunnels holding the switch and exit switch, and get back out without letting the rocket hit you. It's really easier than it looks, if you know a few tricks. This way seems the most harmless:

1. Drop down to the right and get the first switch inside of the alcove.
2. Run to the left towards the rocket launcher, and jump when you hit the slope.
3. Control your jump so that you end up next to the wall right under the exit switch.
4. Walljump off, and land on the slope to the right. Here's the hard part:
5. Slide a bit down the little slope, letting the rocket pass above your head and hit the wall.
6. Jump up and open the switch that lets you get to the door.
7. Travel down and into the door. Congratulations!

Yeah nevermore, thats exactly what I do aswell, until you eventually complete the level. Its weird, doing it this way, you remember playing every single hard level...because you spent so much time doing it...

Definitely. I could recall a few levels inch by inch, but if you described some to me, I'd say, "what?"

The more time you spend on a level, the more possibilities and strategies open up for you, and the more your brain processes it. And it gets imprinted in your long term memory.

Which brings me to a random fact:
When you learn new things, your brain _can_ actually hurt. See, for new information your brain needs more space, so as it creates new nerve endings, it starts to destroy others. The new nerve endings can actually hurt as they grow in, in the same way that when babies start to teeth it hurts. Also, some studies found that the nerve endings that are being destroyed can also cause slight pain.
So, next time you haven't done your math homework and the teacher asks you why not, you can just say, "My brain hurt." And then whip out this in depth explanation on their ass. They'll never know what hit them.

Ok, place a launchpad into an empty level. There will be a couple of numbers in your level data at the end after the 0s and 1s.
Find the last two numbers in your level data. They are the x, y values for the power that the launchpad launches you.
If you make the first number higher, it will make the launch pad launch you more to the side.
If you make the second number higher, it will launch you more vertically.
Get it?

Ok, try playing around with just ONE tile. Play with symmetry. Rotational, vertical, horizontal, inverted. Once you get something pleasing to the eye, figure out what you want the challenges in the level to be. Should it be a race? A puzzle? An action map?
Once you've gotten that, you must play through the map and actually see what kinds of jumps and moves you can make on the tileset. Modify it to improve the flow.
Figure out what would work best as challenges. Should it be rocket based? Thwump based? A mixture?
Then proceed, and place gold to please the eye.

This is happening, guys. No more procrastination.
Here goes: A series of collaboration maps.
The next person to post gets to continue on the map I've made, and I'll PM it to them.
You are allowed to do a section 23 to 92 tiles in area. 23 tiles is one full column, from top to bottom, one tile wide. 92 is a column from top to bottom 4 tiles wide.
Use these tiles wisely, and make sure you don't go over the limit. This doesn't have to be a room map, and I'd like it not to be. I suggest you first decide what section you want to create, and then add appropriate items and tiles. So, here we go!
When you post and you don't want to be a part of this, say that in your post please.
And please be prepared to wait a little while to get the map PMed to you.
Once we fill up a full map, I will create a username; you guys can choose what it's called. We will submit our collaboration maps with that username.

So let's start working! By the way, I haven't finished my section, so the next person will have to wait a half hour or so...

If you wish to edit or veto a section or addition, you may do so, but only after asking the person who added that. If that person says no, and you still strongly believe that this correction should be made, post the map on this page.
Yay!

#71474 5 2005-06-01T14:24:03Z nevermore
Alright, here goes. A rightward moving backwards thwump is easily placed in the wall. Same with moving down - just place it facing up in a full wall.
Moving left and up is more complicated. The easiest way to do it is to manually change the code. So, stick a thwump facing right into a wall. Go back to the debug menu, and find the last piece of code. The first two numbers after the [^] are the coordinates. Take the first one, and subtract one from it.
For one that moves up, place one facing down and subtract one from the second number after the [^].

#72634 41 2005-06-05T23:01:48Z nevermore
Alright, here's my story.

I get a school computer. This is three years ago, mind you.
Everything's going fine, until my friend accidentally drops the computer off of her loft bed. I get a new one. That's one down the drain.
I use that computer for the next two years. Everything is great. One day, some jerk off decides to steal my computer. There it goes. 2000 dollars down the drain. Here comes my second computer.
Because this was about five weeks before school ended, my school decided not to opt for a new computer. I start using my mom's Ibook. It's a pretty great computer, compared to my old one. I have it for about three weeks, and one day the backlight decides to sputter and die. It's entirely broken. When I open it, it looks like a sideways barcode. Third computer's gone.
So there's a week of school left, and then finals. I use my mom's work computer, a Powerbook which has nothing but work things. On the third day of using it, the backlight dies. I take it home and open it, and it's still not working. My Dad comes home. I explain the problem, and he examines the computer. He whacks it, and it starts to work again.
I'm sitting at my desk, using it, when all of a sudden the backlight fails again. I open up the keyboard, and listen. A little black box is whirring like mad. I'm so frustrated, so I start whacking it, hoping it starts to work again. It doesn't. I leave it for the next five or so hours, and I check again. It works.
I go to check the NTTS demos, and there's nothing in the attachments. End of story.

I had a really crazy day today. It started out alright - My friends and I went to a friend's house, we saw a movie. We went outside for a walk and found a shopping cart in front of my friend's house, and decided to mess around with it.
My friend jumped in and I was pushing him around. We were going down a small downhill section when it hit a bump and I accidentally let go of the shopping cart. It's going relatively quickly, and turns towards a street sign, and ends up whacking into it, my friend still inside. Dazed, he gets out of the shopping cart. He's fine. A fairly obese woman near us has a dog. She just locked up her shop a couple of yards from the street sign.
"You assholes!" She yells at us. She seems to like the word asshole. She approaches my friend - the girl whose house we were at in the first place.
"You asshole. You guys are all assholes. You know, you could have broken your head open. You could have hurt someone."
My friend retaliates. "I'm sorry for what happened, but I had nothing to do with it. I wasn't pushing the cart or anything, just walking with my friends."
She says, "But they're your friends, right? So you're an asshole too."
The three other people with us leave towards a school playground we like messing around in.
I approach the woman. "This was totally my fault, and I take full responsibility. It was an accident, and I just dropped the cart. I'm really sorry, but it seems no damage was done, right?"
"You guys are such assholes!" Gee. She's persistent, eh?
My friend says, "Alright, fine, we're complete and total assholes because we made an honest mistake, right?" She gets called an asshole again. "Right, I'll just get it tattooed on my forehead, alright, 'I'm an asshole!'"
She retaliates. "Why are you giving me this sarcasm? I don't need this. What's your mother's name?"
"I'm not going to tell you her name."
"Yeah, that's because you know you're an asshole."
"Look, I'm sorry for what happ--" she gets interrupted.
"I don't want an apology."
"Well... What do you want us to say?"
"Admit that you're assholes."
I cut in. "Fine, we're assholes. Whatever, you can say whatever you like about us, but it's not true. Nobody and nothing was harmed, right? But that's great, we're total assholes."
We walk away from each other, she's still yelling at us, calling us assholes.
We screw around in the school yard, and get bored, so start walking back towards our friend's house. We still have the cart. We pass assholelady. She approaches the same friend again from behind.
"You know if you hit a car or anything you're going to be in serious trouble. That cart doesn't belong to you, it's illegal. I might call the cops."
I jump in again, saying, "Yeah, the grocery store is right up there. We're returning it now."
"Shut up you fucking liars!"
At this point another friend walks up, and says, "what right do you have to call us liars? We didn't do anything other than a simple mistake."
"I can call you whatever the fuck I want to, thank you very much!" She lunges at him, and he runs across the street. It's only a couple feet wide. He just wants to get away from the assholelady. She falls down onto her dog because she missed him when she lunged, and it looks very, very feigned. She gets up, yelling and cursing at the kid. She runs across the street towards him. "You fucking tripped me, you fucking asshole!" She grabs him around the collar, screaming at him.
"No, I didn't fucking do anything." He gets out of her grasp and gets safely a couple of feet away from her. We start going down the street, and she's following us, calling us punk-ass kids, saying she's going to call the cops. By this time we've basically forgotten about the cart. I don't even remember where we left it. She's still following us. I manage to escape, and walk down another street with another friend that escaped. We make it to the end of the block, and call them. The lady isn't with them any more. We turn the corner, and she's coming right towards us. We run away.
We get back to the rest of the group. Apparently, the whole time, she was yelling at them about something or other. These two young women walk up and tell us, "Oh my god, that woman was crazy. We were sticking around to make sure she didn't kill you or something."
We say thanks, and walk away. We realize that she commited third degree assault. We decide to report her to the cops. Apparently, you need to meet the cops in person to report something, so we called them and asked them to meet us on a street corner. It takes them 35 minutes to arrive. They were undoubtedly stopping for donuts.
When they arrive, we tell the story. "We'll keep our eyes out for her," is what they say. They drive off. That's it. That's all the fucking remorse we get for being attacked by some crazy lady.

I was afraid she was going to eat me. *shivers*

#76340 11 2005-06-19T05:54:22Z nevermore
I had another little run in with our favorite lady today.

My friend and I were walking down the street, and we approached the pet store in which she works. My friend wasn't there yesterday, so he had nothing to do with it. He wanted to stop at the pet store, to see what the woman looked like. He went in, saw her, and walked out. He paused in front of her shop window, and she was glaring at him. For some reason he decided it would be a good idea to do a little dance, so he proceeded to do one. She comes out and starts yelling, "Come here, little brat. I want to talk to you!"
We start running away. She starts to follow us. Then we realize - she thinks we stole something. My friend keeps running, so I have no choice but to follow him. We get to his house.

An hour or so later, we meet up with two other friends, both of which were there yesterday. We're walking down the street, and we pass the pet shop. We turn the corner and walk into a deli.
She walks in behind us, and approaches me. "Leave me alone, you asshole. Stop messing with me in my shop, you schmuck. You're all schmucks."
I don't quite remember what I said in return, but it was something along the lines of, "all we did was walk by."
"I don't fucking care. You know, I figured out who all of you are." She points at the one friend who wasn't there yesterday as she says this. "What if I fucking call the cops, yeah? I know your names, so stop fucking bothering me. Never come near my shop again."
She leaves. We all burst into laughter - she was lying through her teeth. First of all, how would she have any way of knowing who we are? Secondly, she gestured towards the only person that wasn't there that day when she told us she knew who we were.
What a bitch.

#78356 4 2005-06-25T13:54:08Z nevermore
You don't have to.

It's called an "NaN" which stands for "Not a Number." This means that something happened to your code, causing there to be an NaN. The most common cause is typing letters accidentally inside of the code. You probably did this. To avoid this, make sure that before you press [L] or [P] or any other key you might press, make sure that you are clicked OUT of all of the boxes. If you are still selecting one of the boxes, the letter will be typed into that box, ruining a piece of the code.

He's right, brickman, lighten up.

Maniac, about the two doors thing. You will not be able to go through if you open the top door first. If you just open the bottom door, you will be able to go through. If you open the bottom door and then the top door, you can still go through.
If there are many doors stacked up, you only have to open the very bottom door, although if you don't want to cheat you can open all of the doors in order from bottom to top.

#86365 274 2005-07-27T16:03:53Z nevermore
Alright, let's get this thing done with.

Map: Viscosity
Author: tktktk

I absolutely love this level. I also think that it's perfect for this competition. It reminds me a bit of manimal lust, although Viscosity is even more stylized and cool. At first it seems difficult, but it gets easier, and it's definitely beatable. An almost perfect map, in my opinion. I could see it as one of the later levels in the game.

Score: 49/50


Map: Sanctuary Revealed
Author: Makron

Another really good level. It's also very stylized, and it seems like a lot of thought was put into the exact placement or certain objects. I didn't really like the gold placement, but that's quite minor. I thought it was really cool that if you played risky you could beat the level very quickly, but if you were more cautious it would be harder. There were a few too many cheap ways to die, though.

Score: 45/50[/color]


Map: Who is Sam
Author: Daddaluma

In all honesty, I really didn't like this map. It seemed very sloppy, and the writing at the top was just stupid. Yes, it did remind me of some metanet levels, but this level definitely needs work. The gold placement was really annoying. Also, I discourage you from makeing entire edges out of [4] tiles. It just makes the level awkward.

Score: 20/50


Map: Crosswire
Author: sweep

The bottom part is very metanet, but it felt weird that the bottom was symmetrical and the top was far from it. I didn't really like maneuvering around on the [8] and [4] tiles at the top, and the fact that there were maybe one or two too many drones didn't really help. Overall, it did end up pretty fun to play, but I found the drones swarming and killing me with no escape maybe too many times.

Score: 39/50[/color]


Map: Day Tripping
Author: sweep

The top was a nice touch, although I'd have preferred it if the gold hadn't gone into the bounce blocks. The bottom was sort of cool, although sort of weird. I didn't like the mid section, though. Some of it relied on luck. A few times I rode up on the thwump only to be led right into a drone. The concept is interesting, though.

Score: 34/50[/color]


Map: I Get Around
Author: Heartview

I liked the tile design, aside from the bottom. I think the layers should have stayed the same size throughout, and that circle seemed very out of place. I might have liked this level more if it were straight up drones, thwumps and floorguards, and maybe a few mines. I really think the laser was out of place, and, if anything, detracted from the level.

Score: 30/50[/color]


Map: Moving Away, but Getting Closer
Author: Echarin

I like the style. It reminds me of tktktk, and tktktk has good maps, so that's a compliment. The style itself wasn't very metanetty, but there are some levels in the game that seem to be - different - and they work perfectly. I think that there should have been wider tiles blocking the chaingun, because I found a couple of times while scaling the wall of death I died, and I had no way of preventing it. Still, pretty cool level.

Score: 38/50[/color]


Map: Fiesta
Author: LouDog004

I didn't really like this map. It's easy, if you don't go for gold, and when it's easy, it's fun, but once I started getting in there and trying for gold it just got annoying. I also don't find it very metanetty. Maybe this would have been more fun if there was one less laser.

Score: 36/50[/color]


Map: Tension
Author: Lancer0

I liked the first half quite a bit. The whole left side was very cool, and might have fit in in the real game. Then came the right side. I didn't really like the right side by itself, and for some reason the lasers ended up on top of each other when I entered the room, which was sort of stupid. I just feel that the right half was unnessecary (sp?).

Score: 32/50[/color]


My computer's acting screwy. I'm submitting this, and then doing the other half to ensure that I lose no data.
#86368 275 2005-07-27T16:50:38Z nevermore
Map: Root
Author: LittleViking001

It's a very cool map. I liked how the bounceblocks helped you collect the gold, although they gave me a bit of trouble with evading the rockets. I sort of disliked going into the pits on the left and right to get the door switch and gold, because you would have to get a certain angle, and if you didn't you would hit a different slope and be sent into a mine.

Score: 43/50[/color]


Map: Palisade
Author: Lancer0

Interesting design, but a lot of things felt very awkward. I didn't like hte ninja's starting place. it meant that you would have to do some strange maneuvering, or just run to the other end, and then jump up the slope. I didn't really understand the door switch placements in the middle - there didn't seem to be a way to get them and still let the level flow. Also, the transition from the bottom to the top felt weird.

Score: 37/50[/color]


Map: Bot Bash
Author: Makron

This is such a fun level, and it's possible to beat it perfectly without stopping. I love how you're always right next to death, and yet it's easy to avoid dying. Gold placement was good, too. The only thing I disliked was that after you got all of the switches and headed back to the exit, you wouldn't be able to go straight up to the switch. Instead, you'd have to drop down to the door and then walljump up. That could have been fixed by replacing the middle top [5] tiles with [3] tiles.

Score: 47/50[/color]


Map: Golden Hourglass
Author: sweep

This level looks very amateurish, but it plays very well. I thought the drone part was interesting, and avoiding the rockets was fun. My only problems for the level were that the tileset design needed some work, and there needed to be some more gold, or the gold should have been in different places. Otherwise cool level, though.

Score: 38/50[/color]


Map: Platforms
Author: Heartview

First of all, congratulations for getting you level into the real game. I actually liked this map, although it tended to get annoying after some time. It definitely needed some gold, but the style was really cool. It was pretty hectic, but I think you used that to this level's advantage. Overall it's fun to play on, although there are a few too many ways to die.

Score: 42/50[/color]


Map: omgz get teh thing!!1
Author: Tsukatu

Very interesting map. I loved certain things, such as the switch on the middle right and left and the top middle section, but I disliked certain things, such as the gold on the bottom left and right. Basically, I think it all boils down to the fact that this style was sort of awkward, and in some places it was to your benefit, and in some places it dragged you down. Overall a really cool map, though.

Score: 45/50[/color]


Map: Turret Arena
Author: Maniak

Too much going on here. I would have much preferred this as an easy laid back level, because the bounceblock/mine/jump pad layout was really cool. But you threw so many enemies in that it just seemed stupid. Also, I disliked the switches in the top left and top right corners. I might have thought they were really cool if they were easier to get - aka less enemies.

Score: 29/50[/color]


Map: Serrated
Author: newt

Interesting design. I loved the fact that even though there was just one gauss turret, it still posed quite a big threat. There were some tileset quirks and flaws, but it may just be a matter of preferrence - I dislike jagged edges. Gold placement was good, and I found it fun to get the switches at the top. The double bounceblocks were a nice touch, although it was hard to get around with the tileset.

Score: 42/50[/color]


Map: Generation N
Author: sweep

Very weird level. I like it. Almost all of the little challenges seemed pretty cool, and even though it wasn't really metanet style at all, I could see it fit in the real game, maybe as one of the earlier levels. I thought the top left area was just weird, and I had a bit of trouble getting out of the tube right below the right facing thwump.

Score: 37/50[/color]


Map: Angularity
Author: holy_trinity/JeR(K)

This map is just insane. It's way too long and crazy to be in the real game, to be honest. I don't have much else to say. The length just ruins it.

Score: 21/50[/color]

YES! Finally I'm FINISHED! I deeply apologize for holding you guys up.
#86369 174 2005-07-27T17:06:31Z nevermore
Some tips for 5-0.
Everyone finds this level hard when they first encounter it. You're giving up to easily. Of course, the easiest thing for me to say is just keep practicing. Of course, that's not helpful.

So, you make it into the middle, and you've unlocked all the door switches. You drop down and release the drones. Panic mode suddenly turns on. Jump out of the little hole, and look at where the drones are. This is the hardest part, in my opinion. The close drone will drop into the pit. Jump over it and land on the other side. Jump out of the enclosed area, and drop down.
<skip ahead>
Bottom right corner, another hard part. The trick is this - you have to risk it. You must go as fast as you can, and to see how to do it, look at the highscores.
You should be home free now.

#92058 15 2005-08-18T03:42:00Z nevermore
Right, example.

My new map, Doublethink.

I spent about half an hour on the original tileset (read description of the map on numa.)
I spent another half an hour trying to make a level out of that tileset.
I realized I couldn't, and spent another half hour adjusting the tileset to my needs.
I spent a half hour formulating how the level will play, messing around with items.
When I have my idea, I place my enemies and the ninja, spending about another half hour.
I playtest the level for another half hour, and find what objects need to be placed to help the ninja move about.
I playtest for a half hour, adjusting things as needed, changing the timing of the drones, moving little things around.
I playtest, playtest, and playtest more. Now is when I add things such as the floor guards in the bottom corners.
I playtest more.
Now I place the gold, and I spend a while making sure it's in the right place, and that the patterns fit the style of the map.
I playtest more.
I spend a while acting very paranoid that people won't like the map, trying to find every flaw and correcting it.
That amounts to quite a bit of time, eh?

I'm concerned about the maps I make.
My distinct style is probably symmetrical maps with an easy linear flow. I've made some maps like that.
However, one of my most important goals is to be versatile with my maps. Some people like open maps that have many ways to beat them. I made some of those. Some people like tight race maps that just require speed running. I made some of those. Some people like puzzle maps. I made some of those. I even made maps in other peoples' styles, just to please everybody. Here's the thing. I'm not comfortable making all my maps in my easiest style, because I feel like that's almost cheating. So I will continue to try to be versatile. However, it's very frustrating when I have a map that was a 'real' stretch for me to make, and people just don't appreciate it. Countless times I've thought that a map was my best, or one of my best, and it ends up with a 3.5/5 rating, and no comment.
Here's my question. What do you guys want? Do you want me to just make my ordinary style of map, or should I keep pushing myself to make quirky or unique maps?
It's very disheartening when a level that I spent hours on perfecting gets rated a C- without anybody who rated it that low telling me what I did wrong, or how I could have upped his opinion of the map.
I await your response eagerly.

#93583 12 2005-08-23T18:19:21Z nevermore
Ok, I just beat the level again. I'll walk you through it.
I suggest you do things clockwise, starting with the top right. So, jump to the right, wall jump up the wall, and jump of so you're holding onto the wall on the left. Wall jump up, and jump off, then quickly walljump again off of the thin tile. Land on the curve next to the floor guard, and jump over the guard. Jump quickly off of the platform. Jump down and land so the guard follows you, then jump up again. Walljump off so that you land in between the two mines, then jump again and get the switch. Jump out, wallclimb up, and jump to the right and get the gold and the switch. Jump off, and slide on the sideways pipe.

Jump over to the right side, wallclimb up, and stand over the drones. Wait until the drone is about to pass in front of you, and drop down. You'll get the switch, and you can climb up the left wall, and swiftly jump out. Slide down, and stand next to the mines.

You just have to keep your cool here. I can't describe this part. You just need to jump through the mines, then jump out.

Here's the thwump part. Jump down and trigger the top thwump. Slide down and trigger the second thwump. Jump to the left, so that you're against the left wall. Get the switch, land on the floor, and quickly jump over the thwump. Land on the wall, slide, and jump up and land on the thin tile. Jump up, get the exit switch, and fall into the exit.

Good luck again.

#94698 69 2005-08-27T19:38:50Z nevermore
Brothers, sisters, mothers, fathers, cousins, nephews, nieces, aunts, uncles, grandparents, grandchildren, distant relatives, gather now, for I have a story to tell you.

Years ago, not a minute more, I was appointed as the attorney general of current affairs. This was a prestigious position, and was only reopened as a bicentennial event. However, nobody understood the drastic measures I had to take to ensure that our freedom would be protected.

It all started one fine summer day, when a small beetle-like man scurried into my office with papers clutched tightly in his hands. I motioned towards the old wooden chair in the corner of the room. He nodded acknowledgingly, dropped the papers on my desk with a sigh, and sat in the chair. He looked around nervously, as if he felt someone watching him. I picked up my coffee, and took a deep whiff. It shot down my throat with an overpowering smell. I sighed deeply, letting the scent leave me. Slowly, I brought the mug to my mouth and blew gently on the thick black liquid swirling inside.

I brought the coffee back down to the table with a noise that seemed to have brought the little man back into this world. He took a deep breath, and spoke. "I have been sent here by the Board of Commissions to report to you our progress in the International Junction Affairs."
I immediately tensed up. I knew exactly what the problem was, and I knew that it was my fault. Hopefully I'd be able to right the wrong on time.

The man looked down at his paper, as if reading from a script, and said, "It has come to our attention that there has been a problem with the Committee of Train Recreation, for--"
I cut him off with my booming voice.
"Mr. Folk," I said, and he was surprised to learn that I knew his name. "I know perfectly well what you and the board are up to, and I will not let it happen. Good day to you, Sir, for I have a previous engagement that I must go to now." I looked at my watch. It was 2:26 in the afternoon. I only had four minutes to do what had to be done. I picked up my coat, tipped my hait at the man who was now anxiously standing, and walked briskly out.

I reached the street. It was a cold winter's day, and nobody was out. I looked around, lit a cigarette, and started walking to the rail road tracks. This was a very delicate situation. I had to make sure that the train could avoid the tunnel without causing utter nuclear holocaust. It was very important that this train didn't enter the tunnel. A report had just come in that all of the energy in the phone lines in the world had been redirected to various train tunnels, and this was one of the worst. The radiation that was within the tunnel was so immense that one'd eyesockets would literally be ripped out if the sat in the train as they went through. Then the radiation would enter their cellphones, and every person whom they had called in the past ten days would recieve the same exact effects as the people in the train, until it spread all around the world.

I broke out in a cold sweat, as I started to jog. I glanced at my watch again - I had two minutes. I looked up as I approached the train station. I quickly clambered up the stairs and hopped over the turnstile. I had to time this perfectly, or I could risk total annhilation. The train neared, and I saw smoke rising from the trees a mile ahead. This was it. The moment of truth. The train let out a blaring honking noise as it came closer and closer. I looked to the right. Not ten meters away was the tunnel, the one thing that could lead to the demise of everyone in the world.

The train was coming around the bend to my left, coming closer. Now it was fully in sight. I got in position to do this. This was my fate. I had to save the world. The train grew nearer as time grew slower. And slower. My mind was racing. Time stopped as my feet pushed against the earth and my body fought against gravity, as I jumped through the air. I flailed my arms in search of something to grab onto, and my hands met the rail on the side of the train. I reached into my overcoat pocket and pulled out a little round blue device, and I clambered onto the top of the train. I threw open a piece of the roof so that wires were showing, and I quickly shoved the circle into the midst of them. I swung the roof shut.

The tunnel was ten feet away, eight, five, four, and suddenly, the train stopped. The passengers gasped in surprise and some were flung forward, but I would later find out that every one of them was alright.

My job was done. I had finished what I had to do. I collapsed in a heap on the roof of the train.

The Truth about Lightningbolts

I know what you've heard. Lightning is a dangerous thing. Never play with lightning, for you shall be blown to smithereen(s)! There was a guy who was struck by lightning seven times, and he lived, and now he's living in misery!
Stop right there. This isn't even near the truth. My friend Dirk and I have done some extensive research on lightning and the origins, and we have come to this conclusion - Lightning is a supernatural phenomenon. There is another elemental plane out there, billions of light years away. Every second a pulse of energy is sent out from the souls of already dead people in every direction. Every so often they are pointed towards us - Earth, thus lightning is born.
You might be wondering how we researched this. Probably our most tedious experiment was when we dedicated over ten minutes to watching the sky, looking at the clouds and observing the changes.
Plus, our pet toad Rachett has been a big help. Each toad has distinct bumps. However, Rachett has just one big bump. Coincidence? I think not. Rachett is a deceased soul that has made its way back to the Earth. Knowing this, we placed slips of paper face up around him, and told him to tell us which one was correct. Each of the slips of paper contained a theory as to where lightning came from. We asked him nine times, and he went to a certain slip five times. We knew we had to trust him.
Not only is lightning a supernatural phenomenon, but a gift. Our ancestors look down upon us and see us suffer, see us in sorrow, they feel they must send something to lighten our spirits. Energy is their only resource. So as not to offend the spirits, we suggest you take this gift. On a storm night, take a clotheshanger, unbend it, and raise it high into the air. Hold a jar in your other hand. Lightning should hit, and travel into the jar. Quickly shut the jar, so your new friend can't escape!
You must leave the jar to sit for at least twenty days, and then open it. Out will pop one of the best friends you will ever have. He can come in many different forms, including a yellow cotton ball with big eyes. You must give him love, and feed him human blood once an hour. He will grow to be a caring and loving pet. Note that we haven't tried this yet, but we are eager to do so on the next stormy night. Rachett just told us it was a good idea.
So next time you see lightning, instead of cowering or being afraid, shake it warmly by the hand. We're sure that it's worth it.

#95486 5 2005-08-30T14:22:19Z nevermore
Corner jumps rely on two things. The angle at which you hit the block, and the timing of your jump. If you hit the block at the wrong angle, the corner jump will not work. If you don't jump at the right time, the corner jump will not work.

I'm sure we all know how to jump. It's just timing.
However, the tricky bit is the angle. To succesfully pull of a corner jump, you need to be on the corner of the block for at least two frames. Practice just jumping towards the corner of a block, and play it frame by frame to see if the ninja's on it for two frames. Practice the angle required to get the ninja on the corner for two frames. Once you've got that down, the timing comes in.
You need to jump on the first frame of those two frames. This is why a corner jump will not work if you are only on it for one frame - on the next frame you're not touching the block, so you have nowhere to jump from.

Does that help?

This has been suggested before many times, and the answer is a definite no. Firstly, it would mess with many, many levels in the real game. These levels weren't designed for that, and if drones could blow up mines it would make some levels easier, and the highscores would have to be reset.

Secondly, this can't be implemented in many different situations. I can think of a couple of puzzle levels that can use it, but it couldn't be used in a variety of ways.

Thirdly, it's just not a very good suggestion. Just in general. It's not that interesting, and most people probably wouldn't use it in most of their levels. And what if someone didn't want the drones to blow up the mines in a level? That would be rendered impossible.

I was struggling with whether to put this in messageboard games or not, but I decided that the heart of the game is really custom levels.
I also had the idea of making this a contest/tournament, but it's so easy to cheat, I decided against it.

So, here goes.

This is a game. It starts when one person (me) names a custom-made map. This has to be a fairly popular map, so that enough people will be at least somewhat familiar with the map. I will not link to the map, because that will invite cheating
You have to recall the map in your memory, and try to reconstruct it tile by tile, object by object without looking at the map. Of course, you can just cheat, but where's the fun in that?
Everyone who recreates the map should post it here in a txt document. Don't submit it to numa, because it's really not an original map, considering the fact that you're copying another map.
Once I feel the submissions are dying down, I will declare a winner (being the person with the map most similar) based on how similar the gameplay is with the original, how similar they look, and if essentially all of the right objects are in there. In reality, the winner will be the one with the map that reminds us most of the original map.
The winner of the last game chooses the next map, and chooses the winner for the following round.
Once again, please don't cheat and ruin the game for us. This has the potential to be really fun, as long as people are honest.

I will start with maximo's map "Flight."

Here's what I believe about street 'art.'

There are two different forms. Graffiti, and Urban art.

Graffiti is focused around tagging, writing nasty phrases, offending/going for a shock factor, and just plain defacing things. That type is despicable. It's not cool. Period.

Then, there's urban art. Urban art is ultra-cool, regardless of whether it's legal or not. An example of urban art is that staircase. Urban art can have a purpose (such as a political or symbolic statement), or it can just be pretty. If I have the money, I'd love to hire urban artists to paint a wall of my house.

Speaking of graffiti, my cousin was in a really interesting ballet production. On the back of the stage were ~five hired urban artists spray painting on a wall that was slowly rising. The dancers did their stuff, and at the end of the performance the wall was finished scrolling, and the artists had created a masterpiece. It was so cool.

#105644 26 2005-10-05T02:57:37Z nevermore
I used to be very caught up with ratings. I cared a lot that people liked my maps. Then I got hit by a huge blow. About ten of my maps in a row were rated something around a 3/5 with no bad comments, and all of them were maps that I absolutely loved. I went through a short period of absolute frustration, and I couldn't believe that all of these maps that I really didn't like were very highly rated, while what I believed was my best map had a 2.5/5.
So I quit numa. Literally. And I didn't just silently fade away, I decided I'd make a big deal about it, and post on the forums how upset I was. Looking back, I think I was a total idiot. Then I started to realize that ratings don't matter. Arachnid, Kablizzy and LittleViking gave me some very good advice.

Now when I make a map, I keep in mind how people will like it, rather than focus on other people liking it. Nowadays I focus the most on how _I_ like the map, and I can honestly say that since I had my epiphany, my maps have increased in quality.

Speaking of internet translators, it's fun to see how they can manipulate and thrash a perfectly coherent sentence into babble just by toggling it back and forth between two languages.

For instance - On babel fish:
Original sentence - My monkey has a male pattern baldness problem.
In Dutch - Mijn aap heeft een mannelijk probleem van de patroonkaalheid.
Back to English - My monkey has a male problem of pattern baldness.
In Italian - La mia scimmia ha un problema maschio di calvizile del modello.
Back to English - My monkey has a problem male of calvizile of the model.

If you continued in a similar fashion, the sentence would get more and more incoherent.

#107434 14 2005-10-12T02:36:50Z nevermore
Dr. Tetris -

Recently I've been having feelings that my life is in shambles. I'm sure it's not the case, because my perception is warped at the moment.
Firstly, let me start off with the fact that I just started at a new school. I'm a freshman. Socially, things are going fine. I can be myself, and I have quite a few friends, and I'm essentially friendly with everyone. However, my grade is almost totally centered around backstabbing and putting other people down. It's not really my thing.
Because I'm a new student, I'm supposed to meet with a 'preceptor' during designated free periods. I missed my first meeting because I had to study for an upcoming test. My next meeting is supposed to be today, but I don't think I'm going to be able to make it. I have very few free periods in a week, because I take two arts, and I try to use them as productively as possible. I hope she doesn't give me a cut.
I'm having academic problems. I honestly feel like there might be something wrong with my brain. I'm fairly attentive in class, and I really want to do well, but I just can't handle homework. It's not that I'm a procrastinator, I quite literally find it impossible to bring myself to doing my homework. It might just be that I haven't settled down yet and gotten into the habit, but this is really affecting how I do in classes. Even though I'm attentive, I don't understand anything that the teacher might be talking about, because I didn't read the assignment that we're talking about. Again, I would use my free periods to my advantage, but I even find it difficult to begin work during that time. Especially considering how few I have in a week. Furthermore, I feel really guilty nowadays because my parents are putting a lot of trust in me academically by not interfering with my work, and I feel like I'm letting them down. I hope to catch up this weekend, but that may be a fantasy.
My science teacher - at the risk of sounding childish - is a total (why is this not in BnT?) meanie-face, for lack of a more explicit word. I requested an extension on a lab report we had due because I was home sick during the class when he was telling us what the whole lab was about, and he treated me like dirt. I quote: "You don't seem very attentive in class, so I've got to seperate the lies from the truth. I've got to figure out what you were spacing out during, and what you actually missed." I'd elaborate, but I suppose to fully understand the situation you'd have to be there.
My family life is, at best, shakey. My little brother is explosive, and I suppose to some extent I am too, and we provoke each other to a boiling point. We end up avoiding each other for a day or so, and then make up. The fact that it's so small-scale is good, but these fights happen very frequently, and it makes for an unhealthy relationship.
I hate my older brother. I'm not exaggerating, I feel utter hate for him when I hear his name. Let me elaborate. He's bipolar, but that's not why I hate him. It's hard to blame him for his actions when it's really only a chemical unbalance in the brain. No. The reason that I hate him is because he has always been a terrible brother. He has made me feel weak, he has inflicted physical pain, he has enjoyed my emotional and physical pain, and he has always, always looked down upon me. I'll leave it at that.
My parents are - to some extent - crazy. My mother especially. She is extremely difficult when it comes to me becoming independent, and I think the reason that's at the heart of it is that she fails to realize the fact that I'm getting older and growing up. My parents know that kids drink, smoke pot, and are irresponsible, and they seem to have accepted that. However, because they understand this, things turn out for the worse for me. A week and a half ago I went out to a party, and I was going to go straight to a friends house to sleep over, just because I live so far away from my school, and it was too late for me to take the subway alone and feel totally safe. I told her about this about three hours before the party ended, and she suddenly started asking all of these questions - where does he live, what's his address, what's his phone number?
She ends up calling his father and making a complete fool of herself (and, not to mention, me). I'd much rather she just gave me a curfew. It's what most of my other friends have. However, my parents are very narrow-minded, and rules they set years ago can NEVER change in their mind. We still have a rule against playing gameboy aside from during trips, which is left over from when the only console we had was a gameboy. In fact, we can play all of our consoles but the gameboy, just because that rule was the original rule. My parents don't understand how accessible the city of New York is, and that I don't need them breathing down my shoulder anymore.
Our housekeeper is next. She's been working for our family ever since we lived in Hong Kong, which was more or less eight years ago. She hates me, and I can see that. There was a time when my brother was having a chemical reaction and he went berserk, and kicked me in the head. Later that night I went to the hospital, but before that I was at home, lying on the floor, clutching my head and screaming in agony. The housekeeper went on cooking dinner, pretending nothing was wrong. She never did help me. When I got my bearings together, I got up, got the phone and dialed my parents - they were having dinner, and they're phones were off. So I called my uncle, my relative that lives the closest to me. He calmed me until I could reach my parents. But I'm digressing. Once, we got in a fight. I don't remember what it was about. I think it was something along the lines of this: my little brother and I were playing around, when she tells us to stop. She's filipino, and she has very, very bad English. I hate it. Eight years of being around only English speakers, and she hasn't learned a thing. I tell her that we're only playing, when she tells me to "Mind your own!"
I repeat the sentence back to her, indicating that it isn't real English. She gets upset. My little brother is upset with her for making him stop playing. I'm upset with her. We fight a little bit. An hour later my parents get home, and she comes downstairs crying. I get yelled at by my parents, and I end up saying sorry to her. She says nothing. In fact, when I apologized, she said, "You know, you have to respect us."
Now I come to these forums. When I first joined, I was fairly new to this whole forum world, and it was exciting. When I recieved modship, I felt great, and things were fun. Nowadays, I sort of feel like taking time to visit the forums is an obligation. I just don't have the passion for this community that I used to have. I feel really guilty for saying this, but it's true. Especially now that I'm a new student, and I really need to focus on getting my life on track, it's very hard to fit in time to come here.
To top this off, I have a complicated quasi-intimate relationship with a girl in my grade. We really like each other, but she's afraid of relationships, because she feels like the breakup will end up in both parties hating each other. Plus, I'm not sure if she's interested. Maybe she wants more of a friends-with-benefits relationship, which I'm not so into. I expect to talk with her tomorrow.
This post seems to have gone on way too long, much longer than I originally intended. It was probably unnecessary, and maybe I'm blowing things out of proportion. It still feels good to let it out, though.

Utter Gratitude,
nevermore

#108518 27 2005-10-15T15:11:04Z nevermore
Alright, I've got a whole load of new maps that I want you guys to see. Keep in mind that this isn't an episode, just a bunch of episodes.

My Gorgeous VIP List: As I made it I considered NC7. If it ever happens, and if the theme is small maps, that'll be one of my submissions. I really like the tiles and the polish.

Dessert: I really, really like this one. There's a bunch of gold as an extra challenge. I particularly like the strategies involved in getting the gold in the rocket/mine area.

Groggy: A pluish map. It was originally fleshed out when I thought the theme for NC7 was going to be maximo maps. I like it a lot, even though it may not be as good as the original plue.

Bing Bong, Avon Calling: I love the tiles on this one. I also love how it plays. It's a puzzle/action map with lots of gold challenges. I like the puzzleish aspect of the very top, and I really like the style of it. I'm not so sure about the upper-left corner - it went through many phases and I think I'm happy with it.

Slave to Lamp: I'm not quite sure what this was inspired by. It reminds me of tktktk's Heroic. I don't really know what to make of it. It's a race/action map that's very queer, but I think I like it.

Unrequited: A mine-field heavy map. It may be too long and hard, but I really like how each individual part works. I tried to keep everything somewhat open-ended, and I think I succeeded to some extent.

Vespa: A drone-heavy map. I don't like this one as much as I like the others, but I still think it's fairly fun. Mostly inspired by maximo's maps, but all in all it doesn't really play like his drone maps.

I've been working on these levels for a month or two now, and I've really poured my heart into them.
So... that's it! Please, I beg of you, play these levels and comment. Some of these I'm considering putting onto numa, but I really need an outside opinion.

My whole life I've been moving around. And it's not some "other side of the district" shit, it's actually moving. Let's take a looksee into my life, shall we?

I was born in New York City, and lived there for all of three weeks. From New York we all moved to Moscow, Russia. We spent three years there, and because I was so young I became fluent in Russian. Then we moved again, this time to Belgium. The most hellish place I've ever lived. Luckily we only spent a year there. So then we were shipped off to Hong Kong, were I spent the majority of my life; seven years. It was the first real place that I could call home in my life. I had great best friends, with the closest relationships that I've ever had. And just like that, we move again. I haven't been in touch with any of my friends from Hong Kong for the past three years. No. This thread is for those people that just don't know what type of map to make/need inspiration/have mapper's block. In this thread, people say what type of map they'd like to see. This can be anywhere from a fast paced action map with a cool flow, to something really specific, such as a close-quarters minefield map.
