Alright, let's get this judging going.

Map: Getting Up
Author: Brickman

Map Quality: To be honest, I don't really like it. It sort of feels like the skeleton of a great idea, but all in all it seems incomplete, both in looks and in play. It feels more like a bug map than a real map, just because of the uniformity of the map; each section is set up the same. It might have felt more like a real map if it were more stylish. I dislike the beginning spot, but the first jump is good. However, with this glitch, you're moving so fast that it relies less on skill to succesfully complete the jumps, and more on a blind tapping of the jump key. With practice you figure out how to do each jump consistently, though, which is good, but it really just doesn't feel like a quality map.

Score: 29/50

Object Use: I brushed on this in the map quality section. While the object use plays a big role in the map, it just isn't very fun. Sure, all the jumps work, and they're perfectly set up to work, but getting them to work isn't very fun, in my opinion. And the object use isn't original, but I appreciate the fact that the map is essentially the use of those objects. All in all, while the thwump catapult works well, it doesn't seem to make for a great map.

Score: 39/50

Total Score: 62/100


Map: X-rays
Author: Lucidium

Map Quality: This here's a very interesting map. I really like the style. It's very visually pleasing. Here's where I'm torn. While to some extent I like the spontaneity, it makes for difficult playing that is unreliable and frustrating. I like how sometimes you can just escape a laser's beam by moving as fast as you can, but sometimes you get cornered, and you do nothing but sit there and wait to die. I'm also not sure if I like the bounceblocks or not. I like the cramped feeling, but it can get in the way in a slightly annoying way. Overall, it's an interesting but jerky playing map with a very cool style.

Score: 38/50

Object Use: I love the unique use of objects in this map. When I first played it, I was perplexed. It's such an interesting effect, and I'm still very curious as to how it works. You get definite originality points. The lasers also make the map, which is also a good thing. However, the way the objects are used makes for a very frustrating play, and it doesn't really flow as much as I would like it to. Maybe if the corridors were wider, it would be more fun to deal with the lasers. I applaud you, though, for getting the effect to work in at least a somewhat enjoyable way.

Score: 42/50

Total Score: 80/100


Map: Bouncy Bouncy!
Author: Hellheart

Map Quality: It's an alright map. Nothing special. It seemed very cluttered, and a few areas were very buggy. It actually felt more like a testbed of effects than an actual level. I didn't like the enemy choices very much, and the level didn't really flow. Plus, each seperate area just didn't work together. Altogether, the level felt messy and thrown together, rather than delicately crafted.

Score: 23/50


Object Use: I have no idea what the unique object use in this map is supposed to be. It seemed like a bug map - just a bunch of effects thrown together into one map. In fact, I can't even put my finger on _one_ unusual use of objects, aside from a thwump pushing the ninja through a oneway, and a jumppad reanimating the ninja after touching the exit (which, I might add, only works in debug mode.) I think the level needed a much more defined theme.

Score: 12/50

That's enough for now.

#111998 2 2005-11-03T01:58:54Z nevermore
I saw it. No pun intended.
I suppose I have negative influence, seeing as my wallet was stolen inside the theater where I watched the movie. My critique of Saw II is about the same as of Saw.

Firstly, I love the idea. I thought the concept was very interesting - not only is the victim physically challenged, it shows the extent to which a human mind will take itself. However, I thought it was executed very poorly. I haven't seen the first Saw in a while, but I remember that I really liked the whole scenario. While the writing was weak, the directing wasn't great and it sort of seemed like a wannabe Quentin Tarantino movie. Nonetheless, it's hard not to enjoy it, regardless of how technically bad it was.
Now for Saw II. I hated - I mean absolutely despised - the scenes outside of the deadly house, i.e. the scenes with Jigsaw and the cops. They were just mind-numbingly monotonous and dull, in my opinion. Because the deadly house was fairly action packed, it made for a jerky flow, and the strange pace made me feel uncomfortable. It's a strange feeling that's sort of hard to explain. I thought the traps were pretty cool, but that was about all I liked about this movie. The plot twists seemed forced, irrational and predictable, not to mention the plot holes that came with them. One of the cool things about the first Saw was that it really took a look into the human mind. With this one, the characters were very flat and stereotypical, and there was nothing interesting or surprising that the scenario made them do. The end came on very awkwardly too. Still, as with the first Saw, I still found myself enjoying it, even though it was pretty bad.

I must say, my favorite trap was the glass box with the razor-blade holes in which the woman gets her hands stuck.

I'd really like to see a very fast race map that's _very_ open-ended. The concept is slightly hard to explain. It's somewhat of a "branch" concept.

Let's say you start off in the middle of the map. You will have four choices - Go all the way to the right, go all the way to the left, fall to the right, and fall to the left. Each of those will give you an opportunity to break off and join another route, or stick with the same route or a slight variation of it. It'd be really cool if this were done with just one exit, and it would require a lot of work on the mechanics of the level. Still, if someone gets this to work, I'll be very impressed.
Note that I don't mean for it to be claustrophobic and physically branchey. I mean that you should be able to get to another section of the map very easily and quickly.

#112933 2 2005-11-06T19:33:17Z nevermore
NaNs have been discussed extensively. They exist because something that's not a number snuck into your level data. Usually this is because when you push [L] to load the level, you still have the text box highlighted, meaning that [L] is read as part of your level code, thus creating an NaN and messing with your level. To fix this, click outside of the text box after pasting, before you press any buttons.

To register here, check this out. It's the top point.

To register on numa, open up N, go into configure, type in your desired username and password, along with your email adress, click create new user, go onto numa, type in the aforementioned username and password and your email adress, check your email to validate your account, and voila.

There're a few ways to do it. Firstly, you can jump down tier by tier, avoiding the thwumps, although that's not very easy. What I do is I manage to get to the top fairly quickly. Once I get the switch, the thwumps are on their way back. I wait for one of the thwumps below me to get right under me, and then I drop down and land on it. If I'm fairly close to the ground at this point, I can just fall off of the thwump and go to the exit, but if I'm too high to jump, I try to drop down another level or two and land on another thwump that's coming back. If all of the thwumps have already come back, I suggest you just drop tier by tier for the rest of the way.

#115331 18 2005-11-16T00:44:37Z nevermore
I support the removal of ratings on numa 100 percent. Of course, it takes away some of the assets, such as the fact that it gives us a fairly solid definition of what a good map is. However, a lot less people were complaining when ratings didn't exist than when ratings existed. And to be honest, probably the reason that I wanted ratings to be removed wasn't because of snipes or unfair votes that I had received. No, it was because I was so sick of all of the complaining amongst all of the one-upping that goes around on these parts. It doesn't make for a fun or healthy environment. It just doesn't. I personally don't look at ratings when I check out a map. If I'm looking for maps that I might enjoy on the main page, I don't look at the ratings. Rather, I look at the pictures. I know what a good map might look like. By the same token, I know what an awful map might look like. It's just as easy.
And tktktk, yes, the end of the golden age was when ratings were incorporated. But don't you see? The _end_ of the golden age was when ratings came into play.

Here's a quick list of the common problems of numa:
Too many bad maps - that's unavoidable. All there is to it.
Nobody comments - rating a map is the easy way out. People rate maps because they want to show they like/dislike a map, and it's fast. While this can't be directly linked to ratings, a part of it could be the mentality that says "why comment when I can just rate?" The fact that there's a much more accessible way somewhat eliminates commenting. Remove ratings, and the only way someone can express their feelings towards a map will be commenting. And if nobody comments, there's always the "Map Commenting Thread."
Snipe votes - simple, remove ratings.
Multiple accounts cheating the rating system - simple, remove ratings.
People not knowing what a map rightfully deserves to be rated - simple, remove ratings.
Basically, almost all complaining will end. Almost.

This is pretty darn close to a utopia, if you ask me.

Anyway, my school? Well, to be honest, I don't have 'a school.' I will never, in my academic career, spend more than four years at one school. I first went to pre-school in Russia, for one or two years, spent a year of Kindergarten in Belgium (Brussels,) spent early Primary School (yep, I went to a British school for a few years) in Hong Kong for about three years, spent the next four years in lower school at another school in Hong Kong (this time American,) moved to New York, spent four years in middle school at a school in my neighborhood, and this is my first year at a new school.

I've had quite a wide variety of experiences. All I remember about my Russia education was that a boy named Mark bit me. That was unpleasant. In Belgium, I remember seeing a slug in the playground. Good times. In Hong Kong, at the British school, I remember a girl in my grade had overcome cancer, and had a shaved head due to chemotherapy. In Hong Kong, at the American school, there was this one kid who made my life hell, always picking on me, making me feel like crap. At my first school in New York, people were idiots. It was a fairly small community (80 or so kids,) and it seemed like everybody was a narrow-minded fool. Since my second school in Hong Kong, I had always, always received gay jokes. Always. For some reason, I emanate homosexual. And not only do I feel bad when people call me gay, I feel bad for the gay community. This is one of the reasons I take so much offense when people use the word gay in a derogatory way. Not only have I gone through so much tormenting, because of it I feel like I know how it must feel to be so oppressed. Think about being a homosexual in this day and age. People use the word 'gay' in a bad way all the time. How hard would it be to come out? But enough of that. I remember on the AIDS walk (a walk to raise money for AIDS research) some kid emptied most of his water bottle on me. I don't remember how he was provoked, but he splashed all of his water on me.
So now I'm at my new school, probably happier than I ever have been. The group of jocks is fairly narrow-minded and idiotic, and occasionally I hear about people teased. Still, it's more diverse than any of my previous schools have been, both in terms of sexuality, and race. Plus, the people there are much more interesting.
In summary, I've grown up my entire life being tormented. It's not fun.

NaN stands for Not a Number. It appears in level data when something that isn't a number is in your level data. It usually messes up something in your level. This is usually because people still have the text box where the level data goes highlighted when they push [L] to load a level. To avoid this, click outside of the text box before you load something.

Map: Dim-N-Tia

Map Quality: The main problem with this map is the fact that it's way too easy to cheat. Another gripe is the cluttered feel of it. It's not a bad map, by any means, it just needs work, both in cleaning it up, preventing cheats, and improving the style.

Score: 28/50

Object Use: The best thing about the object use here is that it basically constitutes the whole map. However, the way this map is set up, it makes for a very cluttered area. The doors are confusing, and figuring out what you're supposed to do regarding the floorguards, and what you're not supposed to do is difficult. The object use isn't very original either.

Score: 30/50

Total Score 58/100


Map: Hunter

Map Quality: This is an interesting map. The rocket works well, and each individual challenge gives you opportunities for speed while still keeping that rocket alive. I like the gold placement, although there could have been more gold dispersed throughout the map. I thought the launchpads didn't quite fit in, a bit weird in this map. Also, I absolutely despise entering the exit tube. It's extremely difficult to make sure you get into the tube with the rocket right behind you, making sure the rocket doesn't hit the sides of the tube.

Score: 36/50

Object Use: A keep the rocket alive map, those are always fun. I liked how all of the areas were open enough to keep the rocket alive. I also really liked how you usually didn't really have to worry about the rocket - as long as you moved quickly, the rocket would stay alive. However, I talked about this in the map quality section, the end is too difficult in comparison with the rest of the map, and the rocket is annoying to keep alive while getting into the tube. Other than that, pretty cool.

Score: 37/50

Total Score: 73/100

Safety Post. I'll be doing this after each map because of my shakey computer.

Apple Blossom - A puzzlish rocket map, made with some help from Lucidium. The title's inspired by the White Stripes.

Cyan - Puzzly map demonstrating gold delay on things other than mines and switches.

Friend or Foe? - Revised - A revision of one of my earlier maps. Nobody seemed to like the original, so I decided to make it more interesting.

#135454 26 2006-01-24T14:40:56Z nevermore
Please, everybody, shut up!
Urgh. This is becoming unbearable. We don't care if you think someone rated your maps down. Firstly, maybe it wasn't a "SNIPZ0RZ OMG!" Maybe it was a mapmaker with very high standards, who decided to rate all of your maps.
Or maybe it was a sniper. And to be honest, I don't really care. I'd say almost all of my maps have been 'sniped.' And I don't care. Why should I? I enjoy making maps and I enjoy playing them. I love mapmaking. Not ratings. It seems, if I may reference Sweep's comment a while back, you love ratings, not mapmaking.
Take a step back. My favorite authors are the ones that expand the realms of mapmaking, namely tktktk, Lucidium, LittleViking001, maximo, blue_tetris, LouDog004, formica, stepself, Sendy and astheoceansblue. There are other amazing mapmakers, but these, in my opinion, are the best of the best. The revolutionary mapmakers, so to speak.
Now let's take a gander at the all author list.
None of the authors I mentioned are in the top three. One is in the top five. Two more are in the top ten. Two more are in the top twenty. One more's in the top thirty. Another in the top thirty-five, another in the top fifty, Sendy, in the top sixty and finally, LouDog004 in the top 75.
The top rated list is full of people that don't deserve to be there. Mostly up-and-coming authors that get high votes because of the influx of new members that rate highly without a clue, as well as possibilities for cheating, and factoring the fact that in general, new authors tend to get higher votes than old authors. It's true, you know it. This is not to insult any of these new authors. This is just an eye-opener.
From this information we can easily draw the conclusion that ratings are crap. Ratings these days shouldn't be taken with a grain of salt, as people these days do not, I repeat, do not rate fairly. Maps are overrated, underrated, and it's all become a chaotic swirl of confusion.
Those of us that are smart have realized that because ratings are so unreliable these days, we shouldn't even pay attention to them. Sure, it makes me feel good to get a 5/5 from someone, but I try to stay objective, and I ponder whether my map actually deserves that. If it seems I recieved a zero, I don't come whinging to the forums, asking Arachnid to ban whoever did it.... no.
In my opinion, doing what I just said is a sign of weakness and ignorance, not to mention materialism. If you'd like, I'll go to the top rated map page and do an analysis of that, but only if you'd like me to.

In summary, we don't want to hear your sniper sob story, as it happens to everyone. Topic locked, and any more topics I see like this will be locked as well.

Feel Like the One - I'm really not sure what about this map you don't like. And I don't mean to be arrogant. I simply would appreciate some clarification.

Havisham - I feel like this map has been very misunderstood. You're supposed to get both the thwumps at the bottom running at once. The trap doors are there to prevent you from cheating, and just running in one end and running back out that end. Drop down onto the bounceblock below the lowermost thwump, and let the thwump go above you. Then launch up and land on the upper platform, run across and fall onto the bounceblock on the other side, letting that thwump go above you and then quickly jumping in the hole. You should have more than enough time to hop in and make it to the launchpad.

Phagocytosis - I think I know where you're coming from here. I do like the mine setup, though, and I also like the floorguard at the bottom.

Yes Yes - Yet another map that I feel was very misunderstood. Maybe I should post demos for these maps.

Polyphonic Spree - I see where you're coming from - in fact, to some extent I agree with you. I'll replace it with another map.

#142777 8 2006-02-12T22:41:03Z nevermore
I have something similar to this. In fact, it really only works if said outloud, because it plays with the fact that "two," "too," and "to" all sound the same. Keep in mind that 2:02 should be said "Two two" in this sentence.

I changed my coffee break from 22 to 2:00 to 2 to 2:00 to 2:02 to 2:22 too, to be the same as you.

It's easier to understand if you think of it like this: the lunch break is a 20 minute break. The guy speaking's coffee break was originally from 1:38 (22 to 2:00) to 1:58 (2 to 2:00). He then changes it so that the break begins at 2:02, and ends at 2:22, so it's the same as whomever he's talking to. Because the person he's talking to's coffee break is from 2:02 to 2:22, the word 'too' means his will be the same as the other person.
Get it?

#149527 71 2006-02-28T02:48:23Z nevermore
Hmm...
I'm going to try and take a step back, and try not to have a close-minded opinion.
All in all, on the cannabis debate, I'm somewhere in between. Marijuana is harmful. This is a well-know fact. But are we really looking at this from a physical point of view? If we think marijuana should stay illegal because of physical effects, we might as well just illegalize cigarettes and alcohol. Marijuana is about as harmful as alcohol, in some cases less harmful. It causes brain damage and memory loss, as well as loss of cognitive skills and depression. Altogether, these effects will directly effect you less than drinking alcohol in the long run. Smoking marijuana is worse for the lungs in terms of equal amounts, but the quantity smoked is different for the two. This also makes this argument shaky at best. But are we really looking at this from a physical point of view? If we are, we must certainly be using some other form of criteria for marijuana than other addictive substances that are legal.
So let's look at this from a socio-economic point of view. Legalizing cannabis would reduce crime rate - dealers would have no jobs, thus eliminating the illegal distribution of it, and people who smoke it illegally would no longer be pursued by the law. This is good. It would also be harder to obtain for kids, as the places that sell it would most likely card them. This is also good, although a bit less realistic, as although generally people are carded while buying alcohol, minors still can get it with a fair amount of ease. Finally, the point has been raised about tax money. People will not be arrested for possession, meaning less tax dollars will go to holding non-violent criminals in prison. This is another good thing.

Now, let's look at the detrimental effects. Firstly, there are obvious physical hindrances that I needn't list, for wont of less clutter throughout this topic. Also, I believe Teh Dude does have a point. Some people are drawn in by the illicit aspects of marijuana, and if marijuana were legalized, what would they turn to? This is not to say that other drugs aren't being taken by minors and adults around the world, but much less that marijuana. This is a scary thought, as they might turn to something much more addictive and harmful. Acid, cocaine, DXM, all of these are more harmful. Will this mean more of an abundance of more harmful drugs?
I'm struggling to list harmful effects on society and economics, as I simply do not know these effects. I'm sure there are more possible tangents, but none are coming to mind. And I'm taking the least objective approach that I can.

I wish I could access the IRC logs. I had a wonderful list on why people decide to smoke cannabis, and why they continue smoking. It was fascinating.
I personally occasionally smoke marijuana. Surprise.
I firmly believe that it's safe up to a point - once it becomes the center of all or most social activities, and it becomes an addiction, (chemical or psychological) there's a problem.
Plus, I have experienced firsthand and secondhand severe depression that is the outcome of very often cannabis. I like to think I've reached an equilibrium in my life, when it comes to drinking and smoking.

If you guys would like, I can try to recreate that list. I'm sure I remember to some extent what I said.

And yes, I did read the entire topic before posting, and I'm fully aware of the fact that some of my points have already been brought up. I'm simply stating my personal beliefs on the matter.

My so-called beef with the Intelligent Design supporters is the fact that they try their hardest to shape and change current science to fit their beliefs of what happened.
The thing about science is it's our best guess as to the reality of things. In this sense, evolution is simply a theory, but the evidence supporting it is far greater than the evidence supporting creationism or any other theories.
Creationists get too caught up in the logistics of evolutionism to see the big picture. Quite simply, the evidence supporting evolution is immense, while essentially the only pieces of evidence supporting creationism are the holes in evolution.

The only real scientific contribution I can lend here is this. Creationists may argue that we can't see evolution happen. This is not true. In small creatures that reproduce quickly, we ::see:: evolution happen. We see natural selection, and we see changes. We are certain of this. To creationists: open up your eyes. Rather than support your argument with slight flaws in ours, try to view things objectively.

After skimming the first page of this topic, I'm going to attempt at making an intelligent post.

Here's my deal. Firstly, I've listened to emo music. In my opinion, it's a load of crap. I can't stand it. If you locked me in a room with emo music playing, I'd sooner kill myself than sit through the music. So that's just to start off. People are welcome to their own tastes, but I dislike emo music.

I also can't stand the label "emo." It's short for emotional, is it not? ::Music isn't music unless it has some form of emotion:: All music has emotion, and to label one form as "emotional" is absolutely idiotic. Also, I believe emo is some of the least touching and emotional music out there.

Another issue I have with "emos" is the total... franchisement of the whole thing. Like blue_tetris has been saying, it's not cool to label yourself in any way whatsoever. You are the product of many different factors around you, and you're absolutely ::conforming::, trying to fit the standards of this "prestigious group."

Lucidium raised a good point - emos walk around thinking they've uncovered the reality of things. They think the rest of us are dumbasses for striving for things, and living life to its fullest. I do believe life is lacking a distinct meaning, but that doesn't draw me from intellectual pursuit. Nor does it let me give up and decide that it's a good idea to kill myself. In my opinion, most emos have no good reason to kill themselves. All I can use to support this debate is what has been used in this topic already.

1. Failing school. Oh, boo hoo. You're unsatisfied with what you're learning, so you give up. Try academic integrity. Try working. Try spending a moment of your life going through actual hardship.

2. Death. One of my good friends just attempted suicide. My godfather died last year. My grandparents are dying, and two of them died within the past two years. My guinea pig died. My brother attempted suicide. Killing yourself is the stupidest thing possible. It just adds to the list of deaths that another emo has.

3. Social problems. Last year was the worst year of my life. I had no friends. The ones I thought were my friends "disowned" me. I felt like crap. This year, I'm happier than ever with my new life. I believe the essential reason I have true friends is because I am my own person. That's right, I exercise ::individuality:: *gasp*

4. Money problems. Ugh. Don't even get me started here. Firstly, like Barabajagal said, money means nothing. That's all I have to say about money - I'd rather not discuss personal experiences here.

My major beef with this emo craze is the fact that it's so manufactured and mainstream. Most people who are members of this group consider it extreme individualism, while it's the absolute opposite. All of you are conforming, trying to fit the qualifications, wearing the same clothes, broadcasting what "group" you belong to. Welcome to the real life, my friends. It's not like this.

The only try way to achieve self-satisfication is if you stop all of your conforming, open your eyes, and realize that being an individual is so much more important than trying to change yourself. Intellectual pursuit and individuality are the two most important things in my life, and it seems you emos have given up on that, not because you truly feel it's impossible, or you have things getting in the way, but because you try your hardest to fit in. You twist and morph who you are just to become an "emo."

That, my droogs, is why I hate emos.

And I apologize for using so much personal evidence. What gets me mad is the fact that they are no worse off than most people in the world, and probably haven't gone through a day of real hardship in their lives. Honestly, neither have I. krusch also makes a good point in saying that emos have no idea what's going on in the real world, where people are starving, being killed unjustly, and actually dealing with true problems. If these so-called emos stopped being such whiney bitches, I'm sure they'd understand that the world is not about them. Pain goes on, and adding more pain, or so the emos call it, doesn't solve anything.

On writing songs and poetry, good on you for expressing yourselves creatively. I write poetry, and I've written one or two songs. Come to think of it, I wear fairly tight jeans, and somewhat tight shirts, and I have long hair. But that's me expressing myself, rather than labeling myself.

Anyone who labels themselves and conforms to fit a label is scum to me. Individuality is the best you can do to achieve self-satisfication.

#159833 68 2006-03-30T18:34:16Z nevermore
I'm one quarter Armenian. My ancestors on my mother's side were Scottish pig-stealers. Make of that what you will. Because my parents are journalists, I've lived in a number of places in my life. I was born in New York, and three weeks later I moved to Moscow, Russia. We resided there for three years, until we moved to Brussels, in Belgium. We stayed there for a year. We hated it. We up and left for Hong Kong, where we stayed for seven years. Now we're back in New York, Brooklyn, and this is our fourth year here. I have never spent more than four years at a school, and I never will, unless I become an undergraduate, or something like that. I don't expect to pursue a career that would require more than four years at college anyway, but you never know.

According to my friends, I oft get very sensitive, but when I'm not I become very "chill." Being chill is a good thing. I dislike being sensitive.

I'm a surrealist.

I'd like a lobster phone.

My greatest opposition is stupidity. I'm highly liberal, although I feel I can't genuinely say that, considering I don't have the right to vote yet. In any case, my parents are liberal. I'm a human rights advocate. Gay marriage, abortion, equal opportunities, these are all very important to me.

I wish human nature wasn't so destructive. If everyone believed in the well-being of others, we could easily prosper in an unregimented society. Every man for himself. It just so happens that humans are selfish, greedy bastards. Thus, we must be kept in line by police forces and governments which tend to be totally corrupt. Humans are idiots.

I used to toy with the fact that I might be gay. I think many people on these forums believe I'm gay. When it comes down to it, I would much rather be with a woman than any man. I feel many guys go through a stage like this in their lives. In other words, until further notice, I'm straight. I'm also agnostic to some extent. Leaning towards atheistic.
I entertain the possibility of the supernatural, but believe nothing without evidence.

I believe people should be allowed to choose what they want to do to their bodies. If they want to sell their sex, they should have the right. If they want to use mind-altering drugs, they should have the right. I believe anything should be legal, as long as it doesn't directly hurt economic or social health. Then again, I disagree with today's society, so economic and social health don't mean anything in my Utopia.
I think we'd all be happier if we walked around naked. Maybe some clothes if it were colder. On hot days, we should all strip. It would be so joyous.

I'm in the middle of a love dodecahedron. At each of the vertices is me.
Oh, did I mention, I hate people who are self-centered.

I hate racism more than most things. Racists should all be shot in the head twice. Stupid whiteys.

#8067 1 2006-04-13T17:22:09Z nevermore
I finally got around to formatting my levels and putting them into a txt document, so here they are. I think I've tackled the episodic feel for them much better this time around. These aren't arranged in any particular order.

nowhere is now: Ride the thwump to open the door to freedom. Maybe too gimmicky for Legacy? I love the level, though.
Usurp: Eh. Kind of complex, kind of awkward. Not sure about this.
Timesplitters: Very easy level. Obviously this would go very early in a column. I like the drone lines.
Digital Entrapment: Kind of easy, quite simple. I enjoy it.
Scarlet Rain: Not sure about this one. It's fun, I think, but it doesn't feel complete, or really good for that matter.
Dupe the Egocentric: I really like this. I love the complexity of the drone paths working together, and the gold at the bottom is interesting.
Genocidal Virus Massacre: Too long and tedious? Maybe.
Oreoplane: This one feels really empty and bland. I wonder what I can do to spice it up.
Gizmotech: Should the floorguard be moved one space to the left? This would make the beginning easier, although it may be a bit too easy without that close call in the beginning.
Sag: I don't really know what's going on here. I created the tileset, decided I hated it, was about to post it on numa as an incomplete level, made some finishing touches, and then realized that I wanted to keep it. So I finalized it. It's still kind of incomplete. Make of it what you will.
Lava Drama: Hee hee. I ask my little brother what I should name my maps often, and for the past couple of weeks his response has been "Lava Drama." So I finally gave a level that name. It's supposed to be like a mouse coming out of its hole. Is the gold too difficult to collect?
Legoland: Very simple, quite easy, fairly fun. In a column this would be an early level.
Noir: Weird, and strangely fun. I started with a totally different concept in mind.
Remorse: Too difficult? Maybe I should delete the mines at the bottom and the thwumps on the side.
Poor Orphans: Totally incomplete. I just gave myself vague placeholders for items and enemies.
Fritz: Just tiles and the ninja. I'll finish this later.
Simple Switch of Syringe: This isn't quite complete. I'm still toying around with the drones. I'd like to delete a couple of the drones and make it so that if a drone sees you, it blocks you from winning, but I'm not sure how to do that quite yet.
Lotus: Too hard? I may just keep two drones in the first block, the rest simple with one.
White Widow: I have no idea.
Foyer: Simple and fun, a little challenging, but not really.
Aluminum Sun Overcast: I love the visuals (turn your head to the left) but the map itself could use some retouching. Advice?
Chalet: Fairly easy. Pretty fun. Don't let the chainguns see you.
War-Torn: Incomplete. I'm using chainguns quite a bit in this pack.
Despot Chalet: I love this concept, and I think the implementation is alright. Maybe it's too similar to Chalet.

#188112 12 2006-06-12T00:14:17Z nevermore
Not ONE person has succesfully explained this to our poor help requester.

Okay. In the game, when you hit an enemy (specifically a rocket, a mine, a thwump, a drone or a floorguard) at the exact same time as hitting a launchpad, you will survive the "death." This is known to most of us as "Cheating Death." In the real game mode, after this happens the only thing you will be able to interact with is the terrain - you will go through all objects and enemies. However, if this happens in debug mode you can continue to play through the level normally, and so this trick is used in many DDAs.

However, when someone gets into the unmoving drone mindset, interesting quirks such as a drone following you into the next room can never be used. Things like that are simply overlooked.
So, yes, it's fair enough for someone to exploit that trick when it's suitable. However, it does close the doors for experimentation and variety, and I think it's a terrible thing to get into the habit of NaNing drones when a much better way to place them is available.

Edit: In response to thecalcgenius: I think you misunderstand. I'm not suggesting that people should encase all of their drones in doors rather than NaNing them. I'm saying it's a bad thing when people reflexively use glitches to keep their drones still, rather than finding a solution to the drone's placement in a more creative way.

#192082 8 2006-06-20T19:26:34Z nevermore
I think this will be my last update. I have a great surplus of maps already, and I'll be able to narrow that down to 42(?) easily.
Uh, so, yes, new maps.

Keel Haul: I like this one a lot, especially the route to the exit switch. The laser and gauss work well together, I think.

Hare Krishna Henna Hookah: Eh. I like the bottom tile structure. The level itself isn't too interesting, although it's fairly fun.

Hip-Hop Alleyoop Saffron City: Jump through the hoops! I like jumping through the hoops. In fact, I think this is one of my better maps. I like how if the laser is in the way of the hoops, it'll almost always finish firing before you hit it. Cool timing.

Pratchet: Elementary little puzzle. I think it's adorable.

Pull: This might be a bit gimmicky, but I still enjoy it. To say the least it's fun to zoom through the... star things...

Unconditional Suspense: Kind of cool, but altogether not that fun. Especially the rocket section. If anything, I'd redo that. Also, generally I die against the wall on the left after getting through the wall of bounceblocks, as the thwumps squish me. I should fix that.

Styleless: Okay, this one kind of sucks. Oh well. It'll be cut, no doubt.

Sanctuary: This is one of my favorites, actually. The chaingun works perfectly, I think, and the drones are pretty cool, though maybe I should open more possibilities for the drone section. Also, the bottom left feels empty.

Federali: Really quirky, really neat. Not much more to say. Love this one to death.

Downpour: I spent a long time tweaking this and making sure that it wasn't just a cool concept, and that it was actually fun to play. I think I succeeded.

Danglemouse: Quite abstract, I'm not sure what to think of this. I like the top left. It's very unorthodox.

Ineptitude: Another crappy one. I'm slipping. This'll be trashed.

Hype: I feel the same way as Kablizzy with this one. The thump mechanism's neat, and the tiles are cool, but it's altogether not particlarly fun. Probably because it's too tense. Maybe just making the switches more accessible would improve it.

Terremoto: Very gimmick oriented, and it requires very accurate jumps, but the fact that there's hardly anything to kill you makes up for that, I think. You have to hit the launchpads at the right angle so it shoots you into the tiles next to it, and then you have to jump quickly, so it sends you flying in the air. Maybe this is better suited for numa.

Pus: NaNed drones!? Yeah. I like this, but we might not allow NaNed drones into any Legacy project. I find I don't have much to say about many of these maps, just because they're generally not as interesting as my earlier expanse maps. Oh well. At the very least, I think this one's enjoyable.

Nazareth's Baby: Novel concept, I think, and it's quite fun to figure out how to get past the rocket. That's all.

Vauxhall: I reckoned I needed a thwump map in the mix. So I made one. It didn't turn out fantastically, but I do believe it's entertaining. I'd like suggestions or edits for this one.

Fulham or Hastings?: Very fun, methinks. I like the laser, and I like how the bottom switch becomes a lot easier to get if you lure the zap drones out. The rocket works well with the drones.

Daddykins: Very Barabajagal inspired, this is one of my best maps in this pack, I think. It might be a bit too hard to get the switch directly above the rocket, though.

Writhe: I had this conceptual map lying around, and decided to shove it into my expanse pack. It's got an interesting concept, but it's probably not special enough to go into Expanse.

Antwerp: This is pretty awful, actually. It can be played as a race on the way to the switch, which at first I thought was cool, but then realized the map just sucks. I'll axe this.

#254015 3 2006-11-13T17:33:55Z nevermore
No, no, the reason the thwump doesn't move here is because it's sandwiched inbetween two [5] tiles. The thwump treats the 5 tiles as filled tiles, because all thwump and drone collisions assume that an occupied tile is a full tile. Thus, the whole row which the thwumps are in is rendered to be filled in spaces, meaning it's just like putting the thwump in the middle of a wall.

Possibly a fluke, but browsing this topic, I feel none of the other responses could apply to me, whereas the one I got is strikingly accurate in describing my life. In fact, more than that, it's as if I wrote it myself. So at least this is an interesting test, possibly even accurate to some degree. At least in my case, it was amazing.

Quote: Colorgenics
You have always been on the move seeking affectionate, satisfying and harmonious relationships. Your ultimate goal has been the realisation of an intimate union in which there could be love, self-sacrifice and mutual trust. It has often been said that 'True love is just around the corner' and - if you haven't found it as yet - you possibly soon will.

The way things are you are under considerable stress and you feel that there is little hope of matters righting themselves. Everyone about you seems to aggravate the problem even more. You feel that at this time you need to be alone and you are right - move back and give yourself a chance to breathe.

You feel that you deserve far more than is being attributed to you, but there is no-one to whom you can turn to for sympathy and understanding. Your pent-up emotions and inherent egocentricity make you quick to take offence, but as matters stand you realise that you will have to make the best of things as they are.

You are pretending that the situation around you doesn't matter, but the effort of trying to conceal your emotions and anxieties is resulting in untold stress. The existing situation is disagreeable. You feel unwanted and lonely and you would really like to associate with someone whose ideals are as high as your own. You want to be above the standard of mediocrity and this need to be needed and that need to need has almost become an obsession. You are trying to magnify the need into a compelling urge. You would really like to tell the world how great you are but no, you are holding back because you feel that your peers may treat you with contempt. This is a great pity because you have in fact a unique quality of character, but the continual restraint that you impose on yourself makes you suppress this need for others and you pretend you don't really care. You treat those who criticise you with contempt. However, to be honest, beneath this assumption of indifference you really long for the approval and esteem of others.

You would like to be respected and valued for yourself and this can only be achieved from within a close and harmonious relationship.

Edit: Colored. Damn good.

#320666 3 2007-05-13T01:04:55Z nevermore
Hehehe. There are two ways of proving that 0.9999... = 1 that I find rather elegant.

Firstly, let's set 0.999.... equal to x.

x = 0.999...

10x = 9.999...

10x - x = 9.999... - 0.999... = 9

9x = 9


The other way, which is even more simple, is this.
The numerical value of 1/3 is 0.333...
3 x 1/3 = 1
3 x 0.333... = 0.999...
0.999... = 1

Anyway, I know you weren't asking for this, but I couldn't resist. ^-^

We don't submit maps on numa to be judged - at least those of us in our right mind shouldn't want our products to just be held under the public eye disdainfully. NUMA is a place for improvement. Just as one comes to an art class to work on their skill, everyone's map-making abilities are always works in progress. We need to learn to respect the creative and recreative process and lower our standards - how can we expect people to churn out amazing things time after time just for our satisfaction? If you dislike a map explain why and be specific, and always stay constructive.

I think this is the cure for sniping.

#17281 1 2007-09-21T01:06:43Z nevermore
The Academy
Sundays 12:00-1:00 Eastern Time every week.
This may sound more officious than I mean, so let me preclude this post with the disclaimer that this will be a low-key project. Acidity and nastiness will not, will never be tolerated.

The Academy is the embodiment of the interactive part of the mapmaking process. It exposes steps of a map in progress to the subjectivity of public opinion. And it's live-action! :Q

:-: Every week at noon (Eastern Time) on the dot we adjourn in #academy on the IRC. My apologies to those of you elsewhere in the world who can't make it. If popularity increases, we might work something out. Call me. ~_^
:-: There will be some sort of direction to start us off every week. Whether it be a theme to follow, an idea to keep in mind or a suggested style, we all embark on a new map.
:-: At 20-30 minutes into mapping we will begin with the first mapper (most likely alphabetically) and he or she posts what he has come up with so far using the wonderful www.pastebin.ca.
:-: After the first person we take ~ five or ten minutes to play the map, reflect, and write down our comments. Comments can be suggestions, appraisal or criticisms, but nastiness will not be accepted. The time limit is a loose boundary. When we're all finished we may proceed.
:-: We each send the mapper a link to the pastebin.ca post that contains our comments in a private PM on IRC.
:-: We have a brief public discussion about our comments and how we felt. Once the conversation is over, we move on to the next mapper and he or she posts his or her map.
:-: A mapmaker can choose to include or exclude any suggestions he or she wants. At least keeping an open mind is key.
:-: We end an hour after we begin, longer if necessary. At this point the finalized versions of the map are submitted to numa and links are pasted in the #academy.
:-: Every week the transcript of the class will be posted in this topic. For privacy's sake, the personal comments will not and cannot be included. However, the guest mapper's comments will, as they will be in the actual channel.

Every week we will have a new guest mapper in to help guide the class. He or she will post his or her comments publically about each map. Our first week's guest will be: Yahoozy.

Involve yourself. This will be really fun and really creative, especially for those people who are having creative difficulties. No sign-up is necessary. Show up at 12:00 Eastern Time on Sunday and stay for as long as you can. Preferrably the whole time.

Discuss!

Quote: scythe33, October 04, 2007 10:18 pm
In Vonnegut's Player Piano, there is a part where Dr. Proteus dreams of quitting his job and living on a farm. That isn't the first time something like that has happened; Biff thinks the same way in Death of a Salesman. It confused me.
What I don't understand is where the farm came in. Living on a farm is close to the last thing I would want to do if I were to leave (today's) civilization to try to live a "simpler" (even though life becomes more complicated) existence. So why farming, as opposed to fishing, hunting, et cetera (which are simpler and don't involve working sixteen hours a day)? Personally, I'd love to shape surfboards, but that'll never happen-oh well.
Of course, I might be disillusioned through direct experience. My grandmother was raised as a Mennonite (think Amish), and her relatives still are. I stayed with them a week, and learned to appreciate iPods, computers, and other shiny things.

EDIT: I somehow put this in B&T. Could someone powerful move it to off-topic?

I think I'm the man to ask here. I'm living on a farm for the second half of this year.

A farm is a place where you get what you put in. Your energy comes full circle when you eat the food you grow yourself. There's something so rewarding about knowing that your work is important to sustaining yourself - when you work on wall street all you get in return for your work is a big wad of paper. Flattering.

A farm is a representation of an idyllic lifestyle. Okay, it doesn't necessarily have to be a farm, it can be a countryside in general. Life moves slowly on farms, things are less complicated by pressures, material things become less important (which is a great thing in my opinion) and you learn to respect the world around you.

And farms are rugged.

End of story.
